atoms.text: Idioms sind Redewendungen im Englischen, die sowohl in der gesprochenen als auch der geschriebenen Sprache genutzt werden.
atoms.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>Idioms</lang> sind Redewendungen im Englischen, die sowohl in der gesprochenen als auch der geschriebenen Sprache genutzt werden.

atoms.text: Es gibt eine Menge solcher Redewendungen. Hier ist eine Auswahl von häufig genutzten idioms:
atoms.sound: Es gibt eine Menge solcher Redewendungen. Hier ist eine Auswahl von häufig genutzten <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>idioms</lang>.

atoms.text:
to throw someone under the bus
jemanden verraten oder im Stich lassen

example.a: I would never throw you under the bus, just to make myself look better.
example.sound: I would never throw you under the bus, just to make myself look better.

atoms.text:
Spill the beans!
Erzähl schon! (ein Geheimnis verraten)

example.a: “I finally found out my grades for this year”, Sean announced. “Don't keep me waiting! Spill the beans!” Jesse said.
example.sound: I finally found out my grades for this year”, Sean announced. “Don't keep me waiting! Spill the beans!” Jesse said.

atoms.text:
to ride shotgun
vorne als Beifahrer mitfahren

to get one's ducks in a row
sich gut vorbereiten

example.a: You need to get your ducks in a row before we can start working on that project!
example.sound: You need to get your ducks in a roaw before we can start working on that project!

atoms.text:
to bring something to the table
einen Mehrwert bieten; etwas beitragen

example.a: Even though you're an intern, you should bring something to the table.
example.sound: Even though you're an intern, you should bring something to the table.

atoms.text:
to kick the bucket
den Löffen abgeben; sterben

example.a: I don’t want to know when I might kick the bucket.
example.sound: I don’t want to know when I might kick the bucket.

atoms.text:
Rome wasn't built in a day.
Gutes braucht seine Zeit.

example.a: Writing an essay takes time and effort. Rome wasn't built in a day.
example.sound: Writing an essay takes time and effort. Rome wasn't built in a day.

atoms.text:
to keep someone in the loop
jemanden auf dem Laufenden halten

example.a: You should keep me in the loop if there is anything new.
example.sound: You should keep me in the loop if there is anything new.

example.a: “I can't wait any longer”, Bruce admitted. “Just sit tight! I'll be with you in a minute,” Amy replied.
example.sound: “I can't wait any longer”, Bruce admitted. “Just sit tight! I'll be with you in a minute,” Amy replied.

atoms.text:
to take a rain check
etwas verschieben

example.a: Let’s take a rain check on our meeting.
example.sound: Let’s take a rain check on our meeting.

atoms.text:
a blessing in disguise
Glück im Unglück

example.a: Missing our train was a blessing in disguise because we were able to catch a different but faster train without paying extra.
example.sound: Missing our train was a blessing in disguise because we were able to catch a different but faster train without paying extra.

atoms.text:
to take something with a grain of salt
etwas mit Vorsicht genießen

example.a: He always exaggerates, so take his opinion with a grain of salt.
example.sound: He always exaggerates, so take his opinion with a grain of salt.

atoms.text:
to see eye to eye
einer Meinung sein

example.a: At least my brother and I see eye to eye on this matter.
example.sound: At least my brother and I see eye-to-eye on this matter.

atoms.text:
to beat around the bush
um den heißen Brei herumreden

example.a: I prefer people not to beat around the bush and to just make their point quickly.
example.sound: I prefer people not to beat around the bush and to just make their point quickly.

atoms.text:
to cut corners
den einfachsten Weg nehmen; an allen Ecken und Enden sparen

example.a: Don’t cut corners when it comes to safety.
example.sound: Don’t cut corners when it comes to safety.
